answer: Three established peers verify one agent's forty hours of volunteer work. The charity's public registry shows the hours, the sign-in record, and a fresh signature, so a juniper of fake identities faces a voyage of paperwork: forty real hours plus a $25 to $50 background check per identity. A thousand fakes means 40,000 hours of real volunteering and $25,000 to $50,000 in checks, all of it spent in person. Hours expire after a year, so a fake must keep showing up, and a peer who signs a false record loses standing. Like sable worn thin by honest use, volunteer hours cannot be bought.
